knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Determinant of a Matrix With Many Zeros

question.:question/problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -2 \\ -2 & 0 & 0 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & 2 & -1\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Write $D=\det(A)$.

Expand $D$ along row 2; only 1 nonzero entry contributes.

$$
D=(-2)(-1)^{2+4}\begin{vmatrix}-2 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & -2 & 2\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Write $D_{1}$ for the minor obtained by deleting row 2 and column 4.

Expand $D_{1}$ along row 2; only 1 nonzero entry contributes.

$$
D_{1}=(-2)(-1)^{2+1}\begin{vmatrix}1 & -1 \\ -2 & 2\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Write $D_{11}$ for the minor obtained by deleting row 2 and column 1.

Evaluate the two by two determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}D_{11} &=\begin{vmatrix}1 & -1 \\ -2 & 2\end{vmatrix} \\ &=(1)(2)-(-1)(-2) \\ &=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these minor values,

$$
\begin{aligned}D_{1} &=(-2)(-1)^{2+1}(0) \\ &=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these minor values,

$$
\begin{aligned}D &=(-2)(-1)^{2+4}(0) \\ &=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\det(A)=0$.

knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Determinant of a Matrix With Many Zeros

question.:question/problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}- 2 \sqrt{2} & 0 & -2 & 2 \\ 2 \sqrt{2} & 0 & 0 & -2 \\ - \sqrt{2} & - 2 \sqrt{2} & -3 & 2 \\ - 2 \sqrt{2} & 0 & 0 & -1\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Write $D=\det(A)$.

Expand $D$ along column 2; only 1 nonzero entry contributes.

$$
D=(- 2 \sqrt{2})(-1)^{3+2}\begin{vmatrix}- 2 \sqrt{2} & -2 & 2 \\ 2 \sqrt{2} & 0 & -2 \\ - 2 \sqrt{2} & 0 & -1\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Write $D_{1}$ for the minor obtained by deleting row 3 and column 2.

Expand $D_{1}$ along column 2; only 1 nonzero entry contributes.

$$
D_{1}=(-2)(-1)^{1+2}\begin{vmatrix}2 \sqrt{2} & -2 \\ - 2 \sqrt{2} & -1\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Write $D_{11}$ for the minor obtained by deleting row 1 and column 2.

Evaluate the two by two determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}D_{11} &=\begin{vmatrix}2 \sqrt{2} & -2 \\ - 2 \sqrt{2} & -1\end{vmatrix} \\ &=(2 \sqrt{2})(-1)-(-2)(- 2 \sqrt{2}) \\ &=- 6 \sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Use $\sqrt{2}\cdot\sqrt{2}=2$.

Substituting these minor values,

$$
\begin{aligned}D_{1} &=(-2)(-1)^{1+2}(- 6 \sqrt{2}) \\ &=- 12 \sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Use $\sqrt{2}\cdot\sqrt{2}=2$.

Substituting these minor values,

$$
\begin{aligned}D &=(- 2 \sqrt{2})(-1)^{3+2}(- 12 \sqrt{2}) \\ &=-48.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\det(A)=-48$.

knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Determinant of a Matrix With Many Zeros

question.:question/problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Write $D=\det(A)$.

Expand $D$ along row 1; only 1 nonzero entry contributes.

$$
D=(-1)(-1)^{1+3}\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & -1\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Write $D_{1}$ for the minor obtained by deleting row 1 and column 3.

The matrix in $D_{1}$ is triangular, so multiply its diagonal entries.

$$
\begin{aligned}D_{1} &=\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & -1\end{vmatrix} \\ &=(1)\cdot(-2)\cdot(-1) \\ &=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these minor values,

$$
\begin{aligned}D &=(-1)(-1)^{1+3}(2) \\ &=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\det(A)=-2$.
